name: Fire, Flags and Records: The Story of the Olympic Games
description: From a sacred festival in ancient Greece to a global spectacle: the Olympics through war, boycotts, protest and triumph.

checkpoints.name: The ancient games
checkpoints.note: Every four years Greek cities pause their wars to gather at Olympia and race, wrestle and throw in honour of Zeus. The festival lasts for over a thousand years.

checkpoints.name: The games reborn
checkpoints.note: The Games return in Athens in 1896 and grow with the Winter Games and fuller programmes. Berlin in 1936 shows how a state can use the Games and how an athlete can answer it.

checkpoints.name: Cold War Games
checkpoints.note: Politics follows athletes onto the field: boycotts, protests and a terrible attack at Munich. Television and sponsors turn the Games into a giant business.

checkpoints.name: The global games
checkpoints.note: Almost every country takes part, and women compete in every sport. Host cities use the Games to remake themselves, from Barcelona to Beijing and London.
